title: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that W_r(k) > k^(ck floor(log2 r)) with c = 10^-5 for all large k and every r >= 2, so W_r(k)^(1/k) tends to infinity for every fixed number of colours, answering Erdos's question. The first lesson proves van der Waerden's theorem with an explicit recursive bound, the digit product, and a Behrend-type colouring that grows super-polynomially in the number of colours. The second proves the tools: a sign-vector count for affine arrangements, binomial tails and the finite asymmetric local lemma, and a prime bound. The third builds a cyclic group with two systems of circle coordinates, a uniform and an adaptive mesh, and counts label words and local patterns. The fourth chooses a balanced outer colouring by the local lemma and proves that every progression is balanced or affine. The fifth adds a sparse random perturbation indexed by boxes and squared-norm bands, and completes the proof.
